name: computeReadiness compute and rcf define readiness CLI
purpose: src/query/readiness.js and src/cli/readiness.js land as a matched pair. The pure module composes computeDelta, computeImpact, the eight gate check functions from TAC-4122, computeCoverage, and the decisions ledger into the single-object contract section 2.4 pins; the CLI is its twin. Text output for readable status; --json for machine consumers and the viewer slice; --check <stage>|all for targeted inspection with the same 0-green / 4-red exit shape rcf audit coverage uses.
responsibilities: src/query/readiness.js: computeReadiness(tree, { freeze, ledgers, profile, testPointers }) returns { tree, delta, stages, nextAction, coverage, decisions, freezeable } exactly as section 2.4 specifies; internal computeScope collects changed + added + impacted ids into a Set; internal composeStages calls each check function in D1..D8 order; internal computeNextAction picks the first failing stage and check; internal deriveTreeSummary shortens the tree hash to eight characters for the tree line.

src/query/readiness.js: computeImpact is called once per id in changed union added; impacted is the deduplicated union of every impact node id excluding the pivots; impactedFbs is the subset with kind 'fbs' AND actionNeeded === 're-execute'.

src/query/readiness.js: computeCoverage is called once tree-wide (strict per-AC, testPointers threaded through) for coverage.tree; coverage.delta is one CoverageResult per unique REQ ancestor of the delta ids (via tree.parentByChild walk to the reqId, or the doc's own reqId field).
src/query/readiness.js: freezeable is true when every stage state in ['passed', 'acknowledged', 'notApplicable'] and false otherwise; nextAction is null when freezeable is true.

src/cli/readiness.js: parseArgs on --json, --check, --help; findProjectRoot; walkTree; loadFreezeRecord; loadAllLedgers; resolveTestPointers; runWithAdmissibilityGate wraps a producer that invokes computeReadiness; on refuse the CLI prints an informational '[warn] readiness: chain admissibility refused (informational; the readiness compute still ran).' on stderr and STILL runs the compute so the diagnostic reports which stage blocks (readiness is a diagnostic, not a gate that hides its answer); the top-level exit stays 0 in that case and --check <stage> follows its normal per-stage exit rule; on ok the CLI renders text (default) or JSON.

src/cli/readiness.js: text output = tree line, next-action line, chip line (D1..D8 with state color words), stage-by-stage failing items (checks with failing ids); --check exits 4 for a blocking stage that is failing, 0 with a stderr [warn] for a warn-with-ack stage that is failing but not acknowledged, 0 otherwise.

src/define/ledgers.js (P3 resolution): loadAllLedgers checks each ledger file's existence with statPath and omits missing files from the returned bundle; loadLedger keeps returning an empty ledger on ENOENT so single-ledger callers retain the ergonomic default.
bin/rcf.js: register GROUPS.define.readiness -> readinessMain; src/cli/help.js: import READINESS_HELP and wire into HELP_MAP.define.readiness + DEFINE_HELP + top-level DEFINE listing.

src/query/index.js: export computeReadiness (plus its subhelpers where useful for tests) so downstream consumers (slice 3 freeze, slice 5 viewer) import through the same seam every other query verb does.

ADR-4126 (0.29.0): fold `levels` and `personas` from `stages[].checks[]` after the eight stage functions run. `levels.intentComplete.ok` is "every productOwner check ok" across every stage (stage state ignored); `levels.intentComplete.blockedBy` lists every failing PO check with ids capped at 20. `levels.readyToBuild.ok` equals freezeable; `levels.readyToBuild.blockedBy` lists every failing check in a stage whose state is `failing` (checks inside an `acknowledged` stage are not blockers). `personas.productOwner.blockers` deep-equals `levels.intentComplete.blockedBy`; `personas.engineer.blockers` is the failing engineer checks in failing stages. `levels.readyToBuild.nextAction` deep-equals the top-level `nextAction`.

ADR-4126 (0.29.0): `deriveNextAction(stages, persona?)` gains an optional persona argument. With no persona it behaves exactly as 0.28.4. With a persona it picks the first stage in D1..D8 order holding a failing check of that persona, then the check with the largest failing list; the command carries `--level intent` on the productOwner variant. `formatVerdictLines(result)` builds the two strings (`Intent-complete: yes/no...` and `Ready-to-build: yes/no...`) shared by the CLI (PR B) and the Readiness tab (PR C) so they cannot disagree.

ADR-4126 (0.29.0): the levels and personas folds are additive; every 0.28.4 top-level field (tree, delta, stages, nextAction, coverage, decisions, freezeable) is present with its 0.28.4 type. No file under rcf/ is created or modified by any `rcf define readiness` invocation. The CLI flags (`--level`, `--persona`) and the viewer tab are PR B and PR C respectively; the compute lands first (PR A).

ADR-4126 PR B (0.29.0): src/cli/readiness.js owns the --level intent|build and --persona productOwner|engineer dispatch. --level drives the exit code against levels.<which>.ok per spec section 3.2 (stricter than --check all on warn-with-ack failures per decision 4); --persona is a display filter that never affects the exit code or JSON content. parseLevelFlag and parsePersonaFlag share the usage-line shape with --check. Unknown values exit 2 with a usage line naming the accepted set. The CLI passes the resolved level into computeReadiness via the readiness context so _meta.level reflects the invocation (null when the flag was absent).

ADR-4126 PR B (0.29.0): the text report prints both verdict lines (shared via formatVerdictLines) at the top; regroups blockers into one 'Product owner: N question(s)' and one 'Engineer: N check(s) blocking' section ordered by the profile register (productOwner-first or engineer-first; unstated and absent profile default to PO first); and renders the per-check line in the per-stage detail block with the persona inside the parenthesis after `over`. --persona X collapses the opposite-persona block to one 'hidden; run without --persona' line and restricts the per-stage detail to matching-persona checks.

ADR-4131 (0.30.0 PR 5): collects candidate paths; the CLI resolves them on disk and passes `resolvedPaths` in the stage context so the `shapes:pathsResolve` check can decide a path:-like token against the real filesystem without turning the gates module into an I/O module. The compute remains pure: readiness.js owns the collection seam; cli/readiness.js owns the resolve-on-disk step before invoking the gate functions.

ADR-4131 (0.30.0 PR 5): the readiness CLI --check policy becomes bite-aware for D3. --check shapes exits 4 on an unacknowledged D3 failure and 0 when acked at the current hash (same recorded-override channel ADR-4124 pins). --check on D4, D5 and D6 keeps the 0.29.0 behaviour until their own PRs (6 and 7) bite. --level intent and --level build exits are unchanged.

ADR-4131 extended (0.30.0 PR 7, spec section 11.6): computeReadiness accepts an injectable `probeRunner` ({ reqId, tree }) => findings[], default null; findings land as probe-ledger entries in the result (merged into `ledgers.probes.probes[]` the gate reads) and count toward consistency:probeCount. With no probeRunner the result equals the 0.29.0 result on the same fixture. src/define/probe-runner.js lands as the seam only; no shipped runner (the harness is the runner through `ledger probes add`). The CLI never passes a probeRunner today; the seam is for test harnesses and for a later harness-driven call site.

ADR-4131 extended (0.30.0 PR 7; R9 amended 2026-10-03, w-2026-10-03-dave-011): --litmus <n> on readiness and freeze requires n distinct litmus readings at the current LITMUS HASH. A litmus reading is a probe-ledger entry whose `finding` begins `litmus:<reader>:` and whose text includes a `hash` matching `tree.litmusHash`. The litmus hash is the tree hash computed with the probes ledger excluded (new computeLitmusHash helper in src/query/readiness.js); the probes ledger is inside `tree.currentTreeHash` by ADR-4120, so a reader writing a probe-ledger entry that referenced `currentTreeHash` would shift the hash it just attested to. The litmus hash is the content-stable hash readers pin to: writes to the probes ledger do not shift it, so n readers can land `litmus:<reader>:` entries at the same hash; writes to the brief, decisions or concerns ledgers do shift it (the content under review has changed). One reader exits 4 naming the shortfall; n distinct readers at the hash pass. No process is spawned and no network call is made; the harness is the runner. `--litmus-attested` remains the default attestation path. Trade-off: litmus readings do not attest to probe findings written after them, which is acceptable because probe entries are themselves readings.

ADR-4131 extended (0.30.0 PR 7): the readiness CLI --check policy becomes bite-aware for D6. --check consistency exits 4 on an unacknowledged D6 failure and 0 when acked at the current hash (the one-line change: D6 joins the BITING_STAGES set in src/cli/readiness.js; the --ack channel D3/D5/D6 already share stays unchanged).

PR 9 (REQ-179 enforcement locus): the CLI computes readiness BEFORE calling `runWithAdmissibilityGate`, passing the computed `stages[]` and the validate-errors array via `defineStages` and `defineValidateErrors`; the wrap evaluates NV-DL-ADM-02 (failing D4), NV-DL-ADM-03 (failing D3) and NV-DL-ADM-04 (non-empty validate errors), honouring --ack-at-current-hash as the recordedInChain override for ADM-02/03. The compute still runs and prints under refusal (AC-17902-4).
internalStructure: readiness.js is a linear composer: 1) compute delta and its docHashes; 2) fan-out impacted / impactedFbs; 3) build stage context (freeze, delta, scope, ledgers, profile, validateErrors, probeOpenCount, coverageTree); 4) call the eight check functions; 5) fold freezeable and nextAction. The CLI parses flags, loads the tree once, loads the four ledgers and the freeze record once, computes the readiness, then routes to the text or JSON emitter. --check maps its argument to the STAGE_SHORT_NAMES map (brief -> D1 ... freeze -> D8) or accepts D1..D8 directly. The runWithAdmissibilityGate wrap sits inside main so refusals ride the same exit path as coverage's admissibility refusals.

interfaces.name: deriveLevels
interfaces.description: [draft] Fold the two levels (intentComplete, readyToBuild) from `stages[].checks[]` (ADR-4126, proposal section 2.1).

interfaces.name: derivePersonas
interfaces.description: [draft] Fold the `personas` block; productOwner.blockers deep-equals levels.intentComplete.blockedBy; engineer.blockers is the failing engineer checks in failing stages.

interfaces.name: deriveNextAction
interfaces.description: [draft] Pick the first failing stage (optionally persona-filtered); carries `--level intent` on the productOwner variant.

interfaces.name: formatVerdictLines
interfaces.description: [draft] Build the two verdict strings (Intent-complete and Ready-to-build) shared by the CLI and the Readiness tab so the two surfaces cannot disagree.

interfaces.name: parseLevelFlag
interfaces.description: [draft] Validate --level against the closed value set (intent | build); return 'intent' | 'build' | null (flag absent) or throw a usage error for an unknown value (CLI maps the throw to exit 2 with a stderr usage line).

interfaces.name: parsePersonaFlag
interfaces.description: [draft] Validate --persona against the closed value set (productOwner | engineer); return the value or null (flag absent) or throw a usage error for an unknown value.

interfaces.name: parseLitmusFlag
interfaces.description: [draft] moduleApi (authoredAt: D3): parseLitmusFlag(raw) parses --litmus <n> as a positive integer; returns null (flag absent) or throws a usage error for a non-integer or non-positive value (0.30.0 PR 7, ADR-4131 extended).

interfaces.name: countLitmusReadersAtHash
interfaces.description: [draft] moduleApi (authoredAt: D3): countLitmusReadersAtHash(ledgers, hash) returns the set of distinct reader ids extracted from probe-ledger entries whose `finding` begins `litmus:<reader>:` and whose text includes `hash` (0.30.0 PR 7). Pure. The CLI exits 4 when the set size is below --litmus <n>. `hash` is `tree.litmusHash` (ADR-4131 extended R9, w-2026-10-03-dave-011), not `tree.currentTreeHash`: the probes ledger is inside currentTreeHash by ADR-4120, so a reader writing a probe-ledger entry that referenced currentTreeHash would shift the hash it just attested to.

interfaces.name: computeLitmusHash
interfaces.description: [draft] moduleApi (authoredAt: D3): computeLitmusHash(tree, ledgers) returns the tree hash (`sha256:<hex>`) recomputed with the probes ledger excluded (ADR-4131 extended R9, w-2026-10-03-dave-011). Reuses hashDocument and computeTreeHash from src/query/delta.js. Pure. The result is stable under writes to the probes ledger (so n readers can pin litmus entries to the same hash) and shifts the same way currentTreeHash shifts under writes to the brief, decisions or concerns ledgers (which do change what the readers were attesting to).

interfaces.name: probeRunner
interfaces.description: [draft] moduleApi (authoredAt: D3): injectable runner shape `({ reqId, tree }) => findings[]`, default null. computeReadiness calls the runner (when set) over every REQ in scope and merges the returned findings into ledgers.probes.probes[] so the gate reads them (0.30.0 PR 7). No runner ships; src/define/probe-runner.js carries the seam only. Pure over its inputs; must not do I/O or spawn a process.

notes: Slice-3 hook (rcf define freeze) reads freezeable and stages[].state; --ack <gate> writes into freeze.gates[<gate>] and re-computes readiness. Slice-5 hook (viewer) fetches the same JSON object over the existing tab wire and renders the pill vocabulary + findings-list + diff components. Performance seam: computeImpact per id on a whole-tree delta (before freeze) may be quadratic on very large trees; the compute stays fast on the dogfood chain (~700 documents, sub-second) but the CLI notes the wall time in text mode so an operator can spot regression.
